newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Egeplast hopes to exceed 97 growth target.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Egeplast hopes to exceed 97 growth target.

text.p: Turkey's plastic pipe producer Egeplast Plastic Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S. expects to exceed its 1997 real growth target of 15 percent, a senior company official said.
"The results in the first half show that we will grow more than our 15 percent target in 1997," Kemal Zorlu, deputy chairman of the company, told Reuters.
First half sales rose by 126 percent to 4.3 trillion lira, against 1.9 trillion lira in the same period of 1996.
Net profit rose to 457 billion lira against 393 billion lira in the same period of 1996.
Zorlu said that Egeplast will have similar growth in the second half.
"Our growth rate is higher than the average market growth rate, because our market share is increasing rapidly," Zorlu said.
"Our aggressive market policies will continue in the future," he added.
He said Turkey's plastic pipe and plastic injection products market had a fast growth potential because of demand for higher quality buildings and infrastructure.
The company completed most of its capacity expansion investment at the end of last year and moved the main production lines to a new plant near the Aegean port city of Izmir.

Egeplast increased its annual production capacity to 25,000 tonnes from 18,431 tonnes, with a total 522 billion lira investment last year. Capacity utilisation in 1996 was 89.5 percent with 22,454 tonnes.
Zorlu said they had concentrated on new export markets in the first half of the year.
"The east European and Central Asian countries are our new markets where plastic materials like pipes and profiles have been introduced recently," he said.

Egeplast export sales increased by 154 percent in the first half to 478 billion lira from 188 billion lira in the same period last year. He said the company's aim was to increase the share of exports in total sales.
On the Instanbul Stock Exchange on Monday, Egeplast shares opened at 8,100 lira, up from 7,900 lira on Friday, but closed the day at 7,500.
